label: z/1/p/f/o/q input in the original phase after several y/j/v/k/e/r/g/h/b tokens
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase (95% of mass; never at t=0 or on the delimiter, rare in the copy phase except a little when outputting y). It needs a trigger input token: z is strongest (8x lift), then 1, p, f, o, q. These six tokens cover 87% of mass on their own, but precision is only 8%. Whether it fires depends on earlier context: it is much more likely when several of y/j/v/k/e/r/g/h/b came before, especially y as the first token. With at least 2 such context tokens: dev P=0.25, R=0.58, mass recall 0.72. Requiring more context tokens raises precision (0.51 at >=4) but costs recall. The rate rises with position in the original phase (5.6x at orig_idx 8) and with L, and first occurrences of the trigger token are favoured. The strongest examples are z at the last or second-to-last original position in y-initial sequences. The context dependence looks graded (like a hidden-state accumulation), so no simple boolean captures it well.
